issues.issue: The fall-back definitional hierarchy ("in the Policy described below or, if not defined therein, in the Indenture") plus the opening qualifier "[u]nless the context clearly requires otherwise" leaves it open which source governs a term used in more than one instrument. The qualifier itself invites argument about when context "clearly" displaces the stated order.
"Commission" and "SEC" are separately defined to mean the same body, and the operative text uses both, leaving a needless duplication to reconcile.

The definition is purely a cross-reference and the citation is garbled ("Section 2.02(c)(ill)"), so the referent must be reconstructed. The intended target, Section 2.02(c)(iii), is nonetheless identifiable.

The definition opens an enumeration with "(i)" that has no "(ii)", so it is unclear whether an intended second limb of the Financial Statements definition was dropped. The omission matters because Section 2.01(h) makes representations about the completeness of these statements.

"[T]he first January 31 to occur thereafter" does not say what it is measured from — the No Form 15D Notice or the stated January 31, 2008 — so the termination date can be read as a rolling or a single date. The whole conditional structure (notice that "no Form 15D will be filed") is hard to apply.

The cross-reference is wrong: "Insurer Financial Statements" is actually defined in Section 2.05(l), not in "Section 2.03()", which is the negative-covenants section and contains no such term. A reader must supply the correct section for the definition to work at all.

The term is defined only by cross-reference to Section 3.04(a)(v), a subsection of the indemnification article, while the operative representation about Insurer Information sits in Section 2.05(e); the scope of the defined term must be imported from elsewhere. If the citation is inaccurate the term has no content at all.

"Material Adverse Change" is defined in terms of a "material adverse change ... which might have such effect" — "might" and "material" set no measurable boundary, and the term conditions a large number of covenants and representations throughout Articles II and V. Parties can reasonably differ on whether any given change qualifies.

After listing three specific documents the definition sweeps in "any other offering document in respect of the Securities prepared by or on behalf of the Depositor that makes reference to the Policy," leaving the reach of the catch-all uncertain. The representations in Section 2.01(m) turn on which documents fall inside it.

The enumerated list of agreements is followed by the catch-all "each other document contemplated by any of the foregoing to which the Depositor, the Owner Trustee, the Master Servicer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee or the Trust is a party," whose reach is undefined. Because nearly every covenant in Article II is keyed to "Operative Documents," the catch-all's scope has real operative consequences.

The definition is framed around "Mortgage Loan," a term this Agreement does not itself define and which sits alongside the Agreement's usual term "HELOCs." Whether Originators relates to all HELOCs or only some loans is left to inference.

The definition makes Premium payable "in accordance with this Insurance Agreement," "pursuant to the Premium Letter" and "in accordance with the Indenture" at once, without saying which controls if they differ; Section 3.02(c) repeats the same triple reference.
